items.title: Two brothers, two divisions
items.short: Wakamotoharu and Wakatakakage are brothers competing out of Arashio stable. Their eldest brother, Wakatakamoto, also entered professional sumo.

items.title: The Koto brothers
items.short: Kotoeiho is the younger brother of Kotoshoho. The pair share Sadogatake stable and both currently appear in BEFN's tracked top-three-division roster.

items.title: A yokozuna in the family
items.short: Hoshoryu is the nephew of former yokozuna Asashoryu, who won 25 top-division championships.

items.title: Three generations of sumo
items.short: Oho's father is former sekiwake Takatoriki, and his maternal grandfather was the legendary 48th yokozuna Taiho.

items.title: Sumo's ironman
items.short: Tamawashi surpassed Aobajo's record of 1,630 consecutive all-division bouts in September 2024. Guinness World Records recognises his consecutive-bouts record. This is a historical record, not a live total.

items.title: When stablemates had to fight
items.short: Toshinofuji defeated Isegahama stablemate Arashifuji in the four-wrestler Jūryō championship playoff at the July 2026 Nagoya basho. Both finished 11–4 in regulation; Shonannoumi ultimately won the title. Stablemates normally never meet in regular basho bouts, but yūshō playoffs are an exception.
